every such ceiling is measured over a simulated reading sequence). §0a maps all eight owner rulings to the sections that obey them. §1 gives the eleven universal moves (PRESENT, HISTORY, PERSON, OBJECT, INSTITUTION, CONTRADICTION, CONSEQUENCE, GEOGRAPHY, TRADITION, OPEN QUESTION, ABSENCE) each with its licensing field under R-DST-B and its six register specialisations, plus CLOSE as a seeded kind and LABEL/POINTER/ROUTE for chrome; eight non-moves (FORECAST, MEANING, VERDICT, FEELING, FIGURE, SAYING, CAUSE-in-the-chronicle, per-entry FRAME); ten wall constraints binding every grammar (STATE before CAUSE, subjunctive edge, ABSENCE never opening or adjacent, BILL never after DEED in one sentence, etc.). §2 sets the closed orders per register with the corrected 1/n arithmetic: dossier level 2 = the owner's four (E1–E4) plus two evidenced openings (E5 head record, E6 material first), level 1 = eight variant grammars V1–V8 with the argument that n must be at least six for the exemplar same-opener band to be reachable; the Herald's G-A–G-E, the ladder's four (with 546 singletons not-executable), the chronicle's per-unit sets (four quiet shapes, letter orders, treaty grid distribution), the DM page's four, chrome's four unit orders and the docent's stated exception. §3 defines the two seeded levels under finite semantics: level 1 needs no new draw (the existing hash-%-length pick over variants rewritten in place in distinct grammars, pool length bounding the grammars, growth only by a new key via chair act); level 2 is a new per-tab mountOrder key with index 0 = today's order, marked owner-gated under THE PROMISE until the fingerprint-inputs receipt exists. §4 specifies the walker: what it reads (tagged grammar, classifier as check, simulated sequences, typed claim sets), what it prints, ten red arms (share ceiling, run, adjacency, the rota arm B3 via successor concentration, claim-set equality as the contradiction walker's grammar face, licence, spread, walls, non-moves, not-executable), and five negative controls (the owner's six-slot template, the rota, the Brackwater block against a two-row open table, today's R1 leaves reproducing 408/708 and 79/708, a fair draw). §5 tabulates the six absence rulings and reconciles them into one law with seven clauses (written only where a typed field holds it; omitted where there is no slot; record writes, apparatus holds the reason; never opener/adjacent/fixed-rate; a declared absence is a starting fact; a new cross-register absence-set arm; tiers by rank are HOW). §6 states the taste-sample requirement (one block, one pool, two variants in two grammars with identical printed claim sets; one tab under two seeds once level 2 exists; the licensing filter shown; absences per class; Herald/ladder pairs; the walker's receipt). §7 carries ten open rows to the chair (Q3/Q4 ceilings, the level-2 gate, the grammar tag's leaf-shape change, the proposition census, singletons, classifier precision, reading-order re-derivation, the cross-register absence arm, Q5/Q19, the docent boundary). §8 records what the file does not do.

clerk.summary: CLERK-LAWS.md written (239 lines, 47,337 bytes; seat line first; nothing validated until the chair's sitting; no corpus byte or dock file touched). It specifies (1) THE INSTITUTION TABLE as a per-settlement, derived, never-persisted, generation-inert projection with eleven typed columns, each mapped to what fills it at product tip 3b1c0eaa5 by file:line (roster + live filter, NPC role/title + the regex-inferred holder link, instantiated service rows for count/collect duties, the banded population, catalog desc/variants/identity for duties, ruin status and impairments for what it does not do, FOUNDED/FOUNDED_UNDATED/PRE_SEED and institutionHistory for provenance) and what is MISSING — measured: no 'bailiff' office exists anywhere; 'whoIsExempt' is null on every settlement (the only typed exemption in the world is a treaty toll term between settlements); persons are a number, never a roll, so the 'closed' flag is ruled PER COLUMN and persons are never closed; two unrelated 'tithe' mechanisms (granary reserve vs clerical levy) must not be conflated. The rule table maps each predicate (holds/counts/is counted/is exempt/does/does not/was founded/quantifier) to its column, and §1.4 walks the owner's Brackwater block clause by clause: refused today on three independent grounds (no office, no count duty, no exemption row) and refused forever on one (the 'only' quantifies over the open persons column); the licensed kicker is the row fact without 'only'. Two live breaches of the same fault in shipped copy are named: RECEIPT_POOLS_DOSSIER_STATE.md:5233 ('the same trades exempt' on a null column) and newsVoice.js:97 ('every household is counted', a totality). §1.7 states the absent-slot decision per register by adopting each reconcile's own absence ruling. (2) THE SAME-ENTRY CONTRADICTION WALKER: reads an entry's sentences against its STATE-KEY/marks, the table, the provenance fence, the bands, and its pool-cell siblings; six typed classes (count vs count; duty vs exemption; state vs provenance incl. pronoun×gender and sustainer×path; modality spent = B-CLAIM incl. quantifier over an open column; sibling vs sibling with the small-particulars allowance; relation gestured at), each with a limb that FAILS (per the chair's 13:22 rule), WITHHELD for the semantic half of R-DST-B, negative control = the Brackwater fixture against three tables (no rows / rows with closed=false / synthetic closed=true) plus positive controls and an anti-vacuity guard requiring it to fail on the four known shipped breaches; it runs at the reconstruction gate (tests/lint walker + the projection's --check), never at draw time (a draw-time refusal moves a seed input — owner-gated under THE PROMISE); its relation to check-pair.mjs is an arm-by-arm table (check-pair is the PAIR instrument; the walker is the ENTRY instrument; v3 = walk(AFTER) − walk(BEFORE)), and to consistency.js/contradictions.js (shares their record shape, not their runtime path). (3) THE CLERK RULE stated once and bound per register in a six-row table naming what 'a field' is, what the kicker is and its licence, the absent slot, and the register's own rule ids (R-DA-15/20, NL-4, H-4/H-11, CL-3/CL-7, D1/D10/D11, CC-6/CC-12), plus five register-invariant corollaries. §4 lists seven owner-gated items and five recorded deferrals; §5 the provenance.
